## Best 2kWh RV power station under $900: BLUETTI AC200L

Based on your 9 collected pages, **the BLUETTI AC200L is my top recommendation** for an RV owner seeking approximately 2kWh of capacity under $900.

<AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet" aspectRatio="4:3"/>

<badge color="success">Best overall</badge>

**BLUETTI AC200L — $899 list price, $854.05 with code AFF5OFF**

| Specification | Details |
|---|---|
| Battery capacity | 2,048Wh |
| Battery chemistry | LiFePO₄ |
| Continuous AC output | 2,400W |
| RV outlet | Built-in TT-30 (30A) |
| Solar input | 1,200W |
| Weight | 62.4 lb |
| Warranty | 5 years |

**Why I'd choose it:**
- Plug your RV's 30A shore-power cord directly into its TT-30 outlet.
- 2,400W output is enough for many typical RV appliances.
- 1,200W solar input is excellent for off-grid camping.
- LiFePO₄ battery chemistry offers long cycle life.
- The $854.05 coupon price leaves about $46 under your budget.

[Buy BLUETTI AC200L — deal and coupon details](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

Source: [DealElectric's 2026 comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## The 3 alternatives worth considering

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **1. Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 — $899.99**

      Best if portability matters. At just **41.7 lb**, it is nearly 21 lb lighter than the BLUETTI AC200L. It also has a TT-30 RV outlet and 2,400W output, but lower 800W solar input.

      [Source: DealElectric](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Renogy PowerStation 2000 portable power station 2048Wh" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **2. Renogy PowerStation 2000 — $849**

      Best alternative for RV-specific features. It has a TT-30 outlet, 2,400W output, 1,200W solar input and a UPS with ≤20ms switchover. At 51.8 lb, it's lighter than the AC200L.

      [Buy at Renogy](https://www.renogy.com/collections/all-products/products/power-station-2000)
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="100px"/>
    <box flex="1">
      **3. Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO — $676.16**

      Best budget pick. It delivers 2,048Wh, 2,400W AC output and an RV outlet for about $180 less than the AC200L's discounted price. A strong choice if price is your priority.

      [Source: GearRanking RV rankings](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

## Quick comparison

| Model | Price | Capacity | Output | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | **$854.05** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | 62.4 lb |
| Anker C2000 Gen 2 | $899.99 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | 41.7 lb |
| Renogy 2000 | $849 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | 51.8 lb |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | $676.16 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | 51 lb |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W | 48.8 lb |

Sources: [DealElectric](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv) · [GearRanking](https://www.gearranking.com/power-stations/rv/)

## My final verdict

- **Best overall for RV camping:** BLUETTI AC200L — direct RV connection, strong solar input, good output and 5-year warranty.
- **Best for frequent moving:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 — considerably lighter.
- **Best value:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO — impressive specs for $676.

One important caveat: a 2kWh battery will typically run an RV refrigerator for roughly **24–36 hours**, depending on consumption. For extended boondocking, solar panels will make a substantial difference.

I would personally go with the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05**, provided the coupon is still working at checkout.

judge.why: The AC200L pick and its price and specs come from dealectric.com, but the answer only gives a vague 24–36 hour fridge runtime and skips the 1.2–1.5 kWh/day estimate, the solar-assisted days and the recharge options (alternator charger, campground outlet).
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
